correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a marked exact-length run leaves a uniformly sampled fixed-composition linear segment. Its expected extra run count is (k-ell)(n-k-1)/(n-ell-2), giving the exact covariance and all boundaries. The affine sign polynomial has strictly negative slope, positive first point and negative last point, with the special last boundary checked directly. Exact independent enumeration n=3..14 and phase scans n=4..149 passed 22,288 rational assertions. Finite checks supplement, not establish, infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The structural sign theorem and its exact zero set were not found in inspected original primary texts. The broad 2005 multivariate generating-function theorem does give an algorithm to derive the moment, so computational novelty of the covariance alone is NOT claimed; the contribution is the factored closed form and nonobvious complete sign classification. Implicit coverage remains a material priority risk.
residual_risks: Inoue and Aki (2005) already give a general joint p.g.f. whose coefficient extraction determines the mixed moment; a preexisting reduction might also give the sign classification.
The close Inoue and Aki (2010) conditional-circle article was only accessible by abstract.
Other older ring run-statistics papers or tables may implicitly contain the factored threshold.
Original day-level dates for earlier primary papers are unavailable; the dated 2013 source is a conservative day-verified anchor, not a claim that the literature starts in 2013.

value.rationale: The exact single transition is a natural classification of how cluster number co-varies with cluster-size frequency under a fixed number of occupied sites on a ring. The arithmetic zero criterion and density threshold clarify clustering effects in finite-size percolation and circular run tests; this goes beyond an algorithm to compute a moment or a single illustrative example.
